summary: Well‑executed preregistered artifactized experiment with excellent provenance and deterministic scoring; however the preregistered head‑to‑head hypotheses about independent generator/repair differences are not testable under the implemented shared_initial_candidate semantics. Manuscript must more transparently map preregistered hypotheses/estimands to the actual estimand measured and include a compact evidence‑to‑claim table and nearest‑work comparison matrix within the five pages. After those targeted, artifact‑resolvable clarifications the paper will be acceptable.
critical_issues: The run implemented preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics that remove independent generator variance; as a result the preregistered confirmatory hypotheses H1 and H2 (about architecture A vs B generator/repair performance) are not testable with the collected data. The manuscript must not present the execution as a discriminating head‑to‑head test of independent architectures without clear, prominent qualification.

The submitted paper does not include an explicit, compact evidence‑to‑claim table inside the five page manuscript that maps each preregistered hypothesis/estimand to (a) the measurements actually performed (shared_candidate vs independent generation), (b) the observed artifact evidence (contingency counts, repair_applied flags), and (c) the consequence for hypothesis status (tested/unobserved). This mapping is essential for readers to interpret the results correctly and is resolvable from supplied artifacts.

The paper lacks an explicit nearest‑work comparison matrix (concise table) within the manuscript that situates the present shared_candidate validator‑parity measurement relative to prior translation→verify and LLM‑agent NetOps studies and clarifies which prior claims remain unaddressed by this run.
required_revisions: Add a concise evidence‑to‑claim table (≤1/2 page) inside the five‑page manuscript that lists each preregistered hypothesis and estimand, states whether it was executed under shared_initial_candidate semantics, cites the exact artifact(s) (execution/analysis CSV/JSON paths and hashes already in the bundle) that support the reported outcome, and declares the hypothesis status as 'tested — measured estimand = validator‑acceptance parity' or 'untested — independent generator/repair variance not exercised'.

Add a compact nearest‑work comparison matrix (≤1/2 page) that lists the closest 3–5 prior works, the axis of comparison (translation→verify vs LLM agent pipelines), and which experimental dimensions (independent generation, repair loops, validator acceptance, emulator/hardware) each prior work and the present run cover. Cite the verified references from the artifact bundle.

Prominently and unambiguously rephrase the paper title, abstract first sentence, and the final contribution bullet(s) so they cannot be read as claiming a discriminating head‑to‑head architectural comparison of independent generation/repair. The paper should instead state up front that this run measures validator‑acceptance parity under preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics, and that preregistered H1/H2 concerning independent generator/repair performance are unobserved in the execution (point readers to the evidence‑to‑claim table).
optional_revisions: Consider adding one illustrative per‑task validator trace excerpt (already present in artifacts) formatted as a short boxed example to aid reader intuition (keep it very short to preserve page limit).

Discuss more explicitly how a follow‑up execution (remove shared_initial_candidate, increase model_calls_used to 240, enable repair iterations) would change power/sample calculations; include concrete resource and model‑call counts that would be required to test the originally preregistered 15pp effect size with independent generation variance.

If space permits, include a one‑line statement on why deterministic validator acceptance reached 100% for the shared candidates (e.g., task difficulty calibration, synthetic task generator bias), referencing representative task generator metadata from the artifact bundle.
